plain_english: Position in this table. 1 is the most severe event of the year. Sorted on severity_C_km2_day, nothing else.
The label the detector stuck on this blob while scanning the grid. Arbitrary, use it to find the same event in the gridded labels array. It carries no ordering.
First day of the event, the first day any cell in it was above its threshold.
The day the event was most intense, not the day it was widest: the day with the highest mean exceedance across the cells it covered.
How many days the event lasted, start to end inclusive. Minimum 3, because CTX90pct only calls it a heat wave after 3 consecutive days.
Land area the event covered on its single biggest day. This is what the 50,000 km2 cut-off is applied to, so anything smaller than about half of Portugal at its widest was dropped.
Average area the event covered per day, over the days it existed. Compare with peak_area_km2 to see whether it was steadily large or one big day surrounded by small ones.
Latitude of the event's centre of mass on its peak day, weighted by cell area.
Longitude of that same centre of mass. Negative is west of Greenwich.
The hottest daily maximum temperature reached anywhere inside the event, on any of its days. An absolute temperature, so southern events win this column almost by default.
Latitude of the cell that recorded peak_tmax_C.

The largest single exceedance in the event: how far above its own 90th-percentile threshold the most extreme cell-day got. Unlike peak_tmax_C this is relative to local climate, so a cool region can score highly.
Average exceedance over every cell-day in the event. Roughly, how far past normal-hot the whole event ran.

units: deg C x km2 x day
plain_english: The headline number, and what rank sorts on. Add up, over every cell-day in the event, the exceedance in deg C times that cell's area in km2. An event scores highly only by being hot AND large AND long, so a one-day national record does not outrank a continental month. It is the gridded version of Russo's heat wave magnitude.
How many grid-cell-days the event contains: cells covered, summed over days. Raw size in cells, so unlike the area columns it treats a small northern cell and a large southern one as equal.
The Koppen-Geiger climate class most common among the land cells this event ever touched, e.g. Dfb, Csa. The event's climate setting in one code.
The coarse group that Koppen class belongs to: tropical, arid, temperate, cold (continental) or polar. This is the column to group by when comparing events across climates.
